text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zambian press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Zambia confederation of chambers of commerce and industry says prohibitive freight charges and corruption on the borders of Kenya and Tanzania impede trade between Zambia and Kenya.
- Zambia has lost its slot at London's Heathrow airport after it failed to reopen the Lusaka-London route which was closed when the state-run Zambia Airways collapsed.
- About 50 Catholic choir members have been rushed to hospital after eating poisoned food.
- The food reserve agency says small-scale farmers need to be equipped with knowledge on crop storage and management.
- Medical doctors have resolved that the Medical Association of Zambia be given regulatory powers to protect the profession.
- The Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa (Comesa) is to begin interviews for a new secretary general after the resignation of former secretary general Bingu Wa Mutharika.
